Policies.Name: Policy IM: EVALUATION OF INSTRUCTIONAL PROGRAMS

fields.Content:
Advancement Via Individual Determination (AVID) is a learning system that provides students with real-world strategies to accelerate their performance so they can succeed in their college experience, career, and life.  AVID has grown to over 8,000 schools worldwide, impacting more than two million students since it began in 1966. Students learn how to ask questions that go beyond memorization and encourage higher-level thinking, providing students with an educational advantage. 

 

AVID layers on existing curriculum, allowing teachers to implement AVID WICOR (writing, inquiry, collaboration, organization, and reading) strategies into any lesson or subject. Students utilize a note-taking process to create powerful study tools. They learn to recognize the most important parts of a lesson, create questions to guide their studying, and revisit and refine their notes to solidify learning. Students also learn soft skills, including public speaking, self-advocacy, time management, and organization. 

 

In the original AVID contract, the District would implement at Butcher-Greene Elementary and Conn-West Elementary in the 2026-2027 school year.  After further review of the AVID Implementation Plan, it was determined that there would be an inequity in access to learning if we did not include Belvidere Elementary and Meadowmere Elementary in 2026-2027 as well.

Approve the AVID quote and amended contract to move forward with the learning and deployment of AVID to include Belvidere Elementary, Butcher-Greene Elementary, Conn-West Elementary, and Meadowmere Elementary. Grandview Middle School, Martin City K8, and Grandview High School are on the original contract and will remain.  The additional expense is not to exceed $54,051.00 for the 2026-2027 school year.

This agreement supports Grandview C-4 School District’s continued commitment to providing students with access to state-approved curriculum aligned with graduation requirements. Through this program, students remain on track to earn a high school diploma while participating in meaningful, real-world, work-based learning experiences.

 

The program establishes a structured pathway for high school seniors to obtain a Class A Commercial Driver’s License (CDL). It is designed to prepare students for entry into the workforce by equipping them with both technical competencies and professional standards necessary for success in the transportation industry.

 

The CDL program consists of a comprehensive 160-hour course that integrates:

  • Online coursework
  • Classroom instruction
  • Behind-the-wheel driving experience

This blended approach ensures that students develop the knowledge, skills, and practical experience required for the safe and effective operation of commercial motor vehicles. Additionally, the program emphasizes industry expectations related to safety, responsibility, and professionalism.

 

Through participation in this program, students gain valuable career-ready skills while expanding post secondary opportunities in a high-demand field.
Approve the agreement with the Zeta Commercial Driving School
$5,100 per student, which includes tuition, books, and related costs (Department of Transportation physical, urine drug test, CDL permit test, final CDL exam, and exam truck rental).

Over the past six years, the roles, responsibilities, and work environment of staff members in the Grandview C-4 School District have undergone considerable change, influenced primarily by the long-term impacts of COVID-19. In response to these shifts and in alignment with the Board of Education’s commitment to supporting employee well-being, district leadership initiated a comprehensive staff engagement process.

From October through April 2026, district leaders conducted Listening Tours at school sites and departments across the district. These sessions were designed to provide staff members with opportunities to share their perspectives, voice concerns, and offer suggestions directly to leadership. In addition, a confidential employee engagement survey was administered to collect broader feedback on staff experiences, engagement, and professional needs.

The data collected from both the listening tours and the survey has been instrumental in shaping targeted action steps focused on improving workplace culture, strengthening communication, and enhancing support systems for staff. A summary of these findings and next steps will be presented to the Board.

fields.Content:
The District is committed to providing instructional staff with high-quality, modern technology resources to support effective teaching and learning. Equipping educators with reliable digital tools enhances instructional practices, promotes transformational learning experiences, and prepares students for success beyond Grandview C4 as competitive and productive citizens in a global economy.

This board item supports the allocation of Apple Laptops for instructional staff across the district. In alignment with the District’s Continuous School Improvement Plan (CSIP), this investment also supports a structured lifecycle replacement strategy to ensure equipment remains current, functional, and effective in meeting instructional needs.
Recommend that the Board of Education act to approve the district purchase of Apple MacBook laptops at a total cost not to exceed $237,600.  (Please see attached quote for specific details.)
Cost of $237,600 budgeted in the District Technology Plan funds.

Regularly scheduled board meetings are set by Board Policy BDA, which states that regular board meetings will be held the third Thursday of each month.  The policy also states that Special Board meetings and Work Sessions can be scheduled as necessary.  Regular Closed meetings are scheduled prior to open meetings. Board meeting dates for the coming year are set as soon as practical so that other school events can be scheduled around Board meeting dates when possible.
 
Additional Special Meetings and Workshops
  1. Schedule a Tax Hearing prior to the regular meeting in September 2026
  2. Schedule a Re-organizational meeting on April 13, 2027 to allow an opportunity for a meet/greet for newly elected members, if any, after the Reorganizational meeting, as well as orientation and preparation time for them in advance of the regular meeting.
Additionally, workshops have been scheduled on various Tuesdays during Board meeting weeks from September through June, using the June date as the annual Work Session date, beginning at 5:00 PM.  These dates can be used for special meetings in lieu of workshops.

The Finance Committee will meet on Tuesdays during the week of the Regular Open Board meeting.

Additional special meetings, workshops, and subcommittee meetings may be set as needed throughout the year.

See supporting documents for the proposed Board meeting dates calendar.
